items.title: PMLA Adjudicating Authority cannot confirm ED's property attachment without judicial member: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday ruled that the adjudicating authority confirming the provisional attachment of properties by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) must include a judicial member. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also ruled that the attachment cannot be confirmed by a single-member adjudicating authority unless that member is a judicial member. The Bench observed that the adjudication carries substantial consequences for the civil and consequential constitutional rights of the person whose property has been attached by the ED. "If the Adjudicating Authority finds that the property is involved in money laundering, the provisions of Sections 8(3) and 8(4) are attracted and possession of the property is taken over by the Government of India. Such dispossession may well endure until the conclusion of the trial for the offence of money laundering, depriving the person of the use of the property for a considerable period before the offence is proved," the Court said. Constitution Day invites easy theatrics. Critics declare the document dead on arrival; loyalists hail the bench as an infallible shield against executive excess. The Supreme Court’s record across 2026 resists both caricatures. Over the past 11 months, the Court has displayed a striking split personality. Envisioned as “Guardians of the Republic,” the Museum brings judicial history into conversation with art, technology and personal testimony, inviting visitors to explore how justice shapes individual lives and the destiny of a nation. Across five galleries, it features more than 280 busts of Supreme Court judges, models of 25 High Courts, 22 language tapestries, 20 interactive biographical pillars and 20 defining judgments, alongside a holographic courtroom and an extensive collection of artworks, sculptures and installations. The inauguration brought together former Chief Justices MN Venkatachaliah , BN Kirpal , S Rajendra Babu , KG Balakrishnan , P Sathasivam , RM Lodha , Dipak Misra , SA Bobde , UU Lalit and BR Gavai . Hailing the occasion, Naveen Jindal , the Founding Chancellor of JGU said, “The Constitution of India is the enduring foundation of our Republic, embodying the ideals of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity. items.title: Saket court acquits former My FM CEO of sexual harassment charges
items.summary: A Delhi court on Monday acquitted Harish M Bhatia, former CEO of My FM, the radio arm of the Dainik Bhaskar Group, of the charges of outraging and insulting the modesty of a woman. Judicial Magistrate First Class Shivangi Vyas of Saket courts held that the prosecution had failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. The Court reiterated that a conviction in a sexual offence can be based solely n a complainant's testimony only if the same is of sterling quality. "The conviction in a sexual offence case can be based solely on the testimony of prosecutrix provided her testimony is of sterling quality that is wholly reliable, consistent and inspires confidence," it said. Where the case rests primarily on that testimony, the Court must scrutinize it with greater care to ensure that it is free from material contradictions, improvements, omissions or inherent improbabilities, the judge added. Since the same was not satisfied in the present case, Bhatia was acquitted of all charges.
